title: Mehndi Henna Pattern Drawing
summary: Mehndi is the art of drawing with henna paste, in a fine cone, on the hand and palm: leaf shapes, curling vines, rings, dots and wave bands are laid out in balanced panels that dry to a reddish brown.
howToPlay: Choose a henna shade and a motif from the strip under the palm panel.
Touch a square to draw there: the same motif appears on the opposite side of the centre line, as on a symmetrical hand.
Copy the small design shown above the panel, then press Check.
rules: The panel is mirrored left to right, so each motif you draw is repeated on the opposite side.
Leaves and spirals lean outward on each side, as they would if drawn by hand along the centre line.
A square counts only when its motif and its shade both match the design; three stars need a nearly perfect copy.
heritageNote: Henna drawing is practised across South Asia, the Middle East and North Africa; artists trace the designs by hand, and styles differ from town to town.
credits: Pattern design: World Heritage Games (original panels after traditional hand and palm layouts)
